readings.subsection: The Campaigns of Judah and Simeon
readings.title: Judah Leads the Battle
readings.subtitle: The Defeat of Adoni-Bezek and Capture of Jerusalem
readings.text: [Judges 1:1] And it came to be, after the death of Yehoshua, that the children of Yisra’ěl asked <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “Who of us should go up first against the Kena‛anites to fight against them?” [2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Yehuḏah does go up. See, <dn>I</dn> have given <dn>את</dn> the land into his hand.”</dq> [3] And Yehuḏah said to Shim‛on his brother, “Come up with <dn>את</dn> me into my allotment, and let us fight against the Kena‛anites. And I myself shall also go with <dn>את</dn> you into your allotment.” So Shim‛on went with <dn>את</dn> him. [4] And Yehuḏah went up, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> the Kena‛anites and <dn>את</dn> the Perizzites into their hand. And they struck ten thousand men at Bezeq. [5] And they found <dn>את</dn> Aḏoni-Ḇezeq in Bezeq, and fought against him, and struck <dn>את</dn> the Kena‛anites and <dn>את</dn> the Perizzites. [6] But Aḏoni-Ḇezeq fled, and they pursued him and caught <dn>את</dn> him and cut off <dn>את</dn> his thumbs and <dn>את</dn> big toes. [7] And Aḏoni-Ḇezeq said, “Seventy sovereigns with their thumbs and big toes cut off used to gather food under my table. As I have done, so <dn>Elohim</dn> has repaid me.” And they brought him to Yerushalayim, and he died there. [8] And the children of Yehuḏah fought against Yerushalayim and captured <dn>את</dn> it, and struck <dn>את</dn> it with the edge of the sword and set <dn>את</dn> the city on fire. [9] And afterward the children of Yehuḏah went down to fight against the Kena‛anites who dwelt in the mountains, in the South, and in the low country. [10] And Yehuḏah went against the Kena‛anites who dwelt in Ḥeḇron – now the name of Ḥeḇron was formerly Qiryath Arba – and they struck <dn>את</dn> Shěshai, and <dn>את</dn> Aḥiman, and <dn>את</dn> Talmai. [11] And from there they went against the inhabitants of Deḇir – now the name of Deḇir was formerly Qiryath Sěpher. [12] And Kalěḇ said, “He who smites <dn>את</dn> Qiryath Sěpher, and shall capture <dn>את</dn> it, to him I shall give <dn>את</dn> my daughter Aḵsah as wife.” [13] And Othni’ěl son of Qenaz, Kalěḇ’s younger brother, captured <dn>את</dn> it. And he gave him <dn>את</dn> his daughter Aḵsah as wife. [14] And it came to be, when she came in, that she urged him to ask <dn>את</dn> her father for a field. And when she got off from her donkey, Kalěḇ said to her, “What is the matter?” [15] And she said to him, “Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the South, give me also springs of water.” So Kalěḇ gave her <dn>את</dn> the upper springs and <dn>את</dn> the lower springs. [16] And the children of the Qěynite, father-in-law of Mosheh, went up from the city of palms with <dn>את</dn> the children of Yehuḏah into the Wilderness of Yehuḏah, which is in the Neḡeḇ of Araḏ. And they went and dwelt among <dn>את</dn> the people. [17] And Yehuḏah went with <dn>את</dn> Shim‛on his brother, and they struck <dn>את</dn> the Kena‛anites who inhabited Tsephath, and put <dn>את</dn> it under the ban. So the name of the city was called Ḥormah. [18] And Yehuḏah captured <dn>את</dn> Azzah and <dn>את</dn> its border, and <dn>את</dn> Ashqelon and <dn>את</dn> its border, and <dn>את</dn> Eqron and <dn>את</dn> its border.

readings.title: The Incomplete Conquest
readings.subtitle: The Failure to Drive Out the Inhabitants
readings.text: [Judges 1:19] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with <dn>את</dn> Yehuḏah, so they took possession of <dn>את</dn> the mountains, but they were unable to drive out <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of the plain, because they had chariots of iron. [20] And they gave <dn>את</dn> Ḥeḇron to Kalěḇ, as Mosheh had said, and he drove out from there <dn>את</dn> the three sons of Anaq. [21] However, the children of Binyamin did not drive out <dn>את</dn> the Yeḇusites who inhabited Yerushalayim, so the Yeḇusites have dwelt with <dn>את</dn> the children of Binyamin in Yerushalayim to this day. [22] And the house of Yosěph also went up against Běyth Ěl, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with them. [23] And the house of Yosěph sent men to spy out Běyth Ěl – now the name of the city was formerly Luz. [24] And the watchmen saw a man coming out of the city, and they said to him, “Please show us <dn>את</dn> the entrance to the city, and we shall show you loving-commitment.” [25] So he showed them <dn>את</dn> the entrance to the city, and they struck <dn>את</dn> the city with the edge of the sword. But the man and <dn>את</dn> all his clan they let go, [26] and the man went to the land of the Ḥittites and built a city, and called <dn>את</dn> its name Luz, which is its name to this day. [27] And Menashsheh did not dispossess <dn>את</dn> Běyth She’an and <dn>את</dn> its villages, nor <dn>את</dn> Ta‛anaḵ and <dn>את</dn> its villages, nor <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Dor and <dn>את</dn> its villages, nor <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Yiḇle‛am and <dn>את</dn> its villages, nor <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Meḡiddo and <dn>את</dn> its villages, for the Kena‛anites desired to dwell in that land. [28] And it came to be, when Yisra’ěl was strong, that they put <dn>את</dn> the Kena‛anites into compulsory labour, but did not completely drive them out. [29] Neither did Ephrayim drive out <dn>את</dn> the Kena‛anites who dwelt in Gezer, so the Kena‛anites dwelt in their midst, in Gezer. [30] Neither did Zeḇulun drive out <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Qitron or <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Nahalol, so the Kena‛anites dwelt in their midst, and became compulsory labour. [31] Neither did Ashěr drive out <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Akko nor <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Tsiḏon, nor of Aḥlaḇ, nor of Aḵziḇ, nor of Ḥelbah, nor of Aphiq, nor of Reḥoḇ. [32] So the Ashěrites dwelt in the midst of the Kena‛anites, the inhabitants of the land, because they did not drive them out. [33] Neither did Naphtali drive out <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Běyth Shemesh nor <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Běyth Anath, but they dwelt among the Kena‛anites, the inhabitants of the land. And the inhabitants of Běyth Shemesh and of Běyth Anath became compulsory labour for them. [34] And the Amorites pressed <dn>את</dn> the children of Dan into the mountains, for they would not allow them to come down to the valley, [35] and the Amorites desired to dwell in Mount Ḥeres, in Ayalon, and in Sha‛alḇim. But when the hand of the house of Yosěph became stronger, they became compulsory labour. [36] And the border of the Amorites was from the Ascent of Aqrabbim, from Sela, and upward.

readings.title: The Rebuke of the Messenger
readings.subtitle: Israel Weeps for Their Disobedience
readings.text: [Judges 2:1] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came up from Gilgal to Boḵim, and said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> led <dn>את</dn> you up from Mitsrayim and brought <dn>את</dn> you to the land of which <dn>I</dn> swore to your fathers, and <dn>I</dn> said, ‘<dn>I</dn> do not break <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with <dn>את</dn> you,</dq> [2] <dq>and as for you, do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of this land – break down their slaughter-places.’ But you have not obeyed <dn>My</dn> voice. What is this you have done?</dq> [3] <dq>“Therefore <dn>I</dn> also said, ‘<dn>I</dn> am not driving them out before you, and they shall be adversaries to you, and their mighty ones shall be a snare to you.’ ”</dq> [4] And it came to be, when the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke <dn>את</dn> these words to all the children of Yisra’ěl, that the people lifted up <dn>את</dn> their voice and wept. [5] So they called the name of that place Boḵim, and slaughtered there to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Death of Joshua
readings.subtitle: The Passing of a Faithful Generation
readings.text: [Judges 2:6] Then Yehoshua dismissed <dn>את</dn> the people, and the children of Yisra’ěl went each to his own inheritance to possess <dn>את</dn> the land. [7] And the people served <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all the days of Yehoshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Yehoshua, who had seen <dn>את</dn> all the great works of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> had done for Yisra’ěl. [8] And Yehoshua son of Nun, the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, died, one hundred and ten years old. [9] And they buried <dn>את</dn> him within the border of his inheritance at Timnath Ḥeres, in the mountains of Ephrayim, on the north side of Mount Ga‛ash.

readings.title: The Apostasy of Israel
readings.subtitle: Forsaking the Covenant for the Baals
readings.text: [Judges 2:10] And all that generation were likewise gathered to their fathers, and another generation arose after them who did not know <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> nor <dn>את</dn> the work which <dn>He</dn> had done for Yisra’ěl. [11] Then the children of Yisra’ěl did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and served <dn>את</dn> the Ba‛als, [12] and forsook <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers, who had brought <dn>את</dn> them out of the land of Mitsrayim, and went after other mighty ones, of the mighty ones of the people who were all around them, and they bowed down to them, and provoked <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] So they forsook <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and served Ba‛al and the Ashtoreths. [14] And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Yisra’ěl. Therefore <dn>He</dn> gave them into the hands of plunderers who despoiled <dn>את</dn> them. And <dn>He</dn> sold them into the hands of their enemies all around, and they were unable to stand before their enemies any longer. [15] Wherever they went out, the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was against them for evil, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had spoken, and as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had sworn to them. And they were distressed – greatly.

readings.title: The Pattern of the Judges
readings.subtitle: Compassion and Stubborn Rebellion
readings.text: [Judges 2:16] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> raised up rulers who saved them from the hand of those who plundered them. [17] However, they did not listen to their rulers either, but went whoring after other mighty ones, and bowed down to them. They soon turned aside from the way in which their fathers walked, in obeying the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – they did not do so. [18] And when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> raised up rulers for them, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with the ruler and saved them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the ruler, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had compassion on their groaning because of those who oppressed them and crushed them. [19] And it came to be, when the ruler was dead, that they would turn back and do more corruptly than their fathers, to go after other mighty ones, to serve them and bow down to them. They did not refrain from their practices and from their stubborn way. [20] And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Yisra’ěl, and <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Because this nation has transgressed <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant that <dn>I</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> their fathers, and has not obeyed <dn>My</dn> voice,</dq> [21] <dq><dn>I</dn> also shall no longer drive out before them any of the nations which Yehoshua left when he died,</dq> [22] <dq>in order to try <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl by them, whether they would guard <dn>את</dn> the way of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to walk in them as their fathers guarded them, or not.”</dq> [23] So <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> left <dn>את</dn> those nations, without driving them out at once, and did not give them into the hand of Yehoshua.

readings.subsection: The Nations Left to Test Israel
readings.title: The Testing of Israel
readings.subtitle: Intermarriage and Idolatry
readings.text: [Judges 3:1] And these are the nations which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> left, to try <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl by them, all those who had not known <dn>את</dn> all the battles in Kena‛an, [2] only that the generations of the children of Yisra’ěl might know, to teach them battle, only those who before did not know them: [3] five princes of the Philistines, and all the Kena‛anites, and the Tsiḏonians, and the Ḥivvites who dwelt in Mount Leḇanon, from Mount Ba‛al Ḥermon to the entrance of Ḥamath. [4] And they were to try <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl by them, to know whether they would obey <dn>את</dn> the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which <dn>He</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> their fathers by the hand of Mosheh. [5] Thus the children of Yisra’ěl dwelt in the midst of the Kena‛anites, the Ḥittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Ḥivvites, and the Yeḇusites, [6] and took <dn>את</dn> their daughters to be their wives, and gave <dn>את</dn> their daughters to their sons, and they served <dn>את</dn> their mighty ones.

readings.title: Othniel the First Judge
readings.subtitle: Deliverance from Aram Naharayim
readings.text: [Judges 3:7] Thus the children of Yisra’ěl did <dn>את</dn> evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and forgot <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, and served <dn>את</dn> the Ba‛als and <dn>את</dn> the Ashěrahs. [8] And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Yisra’ěl, and <dn>He</dn> sold them into the hand of Kushan-Rish‛athayim sovereign of Aram Naharayim. And the children of Yisra’ěl served <dn>את</dn> Kushan-Rish‛athayim eight years. [9] And when the children of Yisra’ěl cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> raised up a saviour for the children of Yisra’ěl, who saved them: <dn>את</dn> Othni’ěl son of Qenaz, Kalěḇ’s younger brother. [10] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon him, and he ruled <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl, and went out to battle, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave into his hand <dn>את</dn> Kushan-Rish‛athayim sovereign of Aram Naharayim. And his hand prevailed over Kushan-Rish‛athayim, [11] and the land had rest for forty years. Then Othni’ěl son of Qenaz died,

readings.title: Ehud the Left-Handed Judge
readings.subtitle: The Assassination of Eglon and Defeat of Moab
readings.text: [Judges 3:12] and the children of Yisra’ěl again did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made <dn>את</dn> Eḡlon sovereign of Mo’aḇ strong against Yisra’ěl, because they had done <dn>את</dn> evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] And he gathered to himself <dn>את</dn> the children of Ammon and Amalěq, and went and struck <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl, and they took possession of <dn>את</dn> the city of palms. [14] And the children of Yisra’ěl served <dn>את</dn> Eḡlon sovereign of Mo’aḇ eighteen years. [15] And when the children of Yisra’ěl cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> raised up a saviour for them: <dn>את</dn> Ěhuḏ son of Gěra, a Binyamite, a man impeded in his right hand. And by him the children of Yisra’ěl sent a present to Eḡlon sovereign of Mo’aḇ. [16] And Ěhuḏ made himself a sword, it was double-edged and a cubit in length, and he girded <dn>את</dn> it under his long robe on his right thigh. [17] And he brought <dn>את</dn> the present to Eḡlon sovereign of Mo’aḇ. Now Eḡlon was a very fat man. [18] And it came to be that when he had finished bringing near <dn>את</dn> the present, he sent away <dn>את</dn> the people bearing the present. [19] But he himself turned back from the stone images that were at Gilgal, and said, “I have a secret message for you, O sovereign.” And he said, “Be silent!” And all those standing beside him went out from him. [20] And Ěhuḏ came to him while he was sitting in his cool roof room. And Ěhuḏ said, “I have a message from <dn>Elohim</dn> for you.” So he arose from his seat. [21] And Ěhuḏ reached with <dn>את</dn> his left hand, and took <dn>את</dn> the sword from his right thigh, and thrust <dn>את</dn> it into his stomach. [22] And the handle went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the sword out of his stomach, and it came out behind. [23] Then Ěhuḏ went out to the porch and shut <dn>את</dn> the doors of the upper room behind him and locked them. [24] And when he had gone out, his servants came to look and saw the doors of the roof room were locked. So they said, “He is only covering <dn>את</dn> his feet in the cool roof room.” [25] And they waited until they were ashamed, but saw he was not opening the doors of the upper room. So they took <dn>את</dn> the key and opened them and saw their master, fallen to the ground, dead. [26] But while they were delaying Ěhuḏ escaped and had passed beyond <dn>את</dn> the stone images, and escaped to Se‛irah. [27] And it came to be, when he arrived, that he blew the shophar in the mountains of Ephrayim, and the children of Yisra’ěl went down with <dn>את</dn> him from the mountains, with him leading them. [28] And he said to them, “Follow me, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given <dn>את</dn> your enemies <dn>את</dn> the Mo’aḇites into your hand.” And they went down after him, and took <dn>את</dn> the fords of Yarděn leading to Mo’aḇ, and did not allow anyone to pass over. [29] And they struck <dn>את</dn> about ten thousand men of Mo’aḇ at that time, all robust and brave men, and not a man escaped. [30] And on that day Mo’aḇ was humbled under the hand of Yisra’ěl. And the land had rest for eighty years. [31] And after him was Shamgar son of Anath, and he struck <dn>את</dn> six hundred men of the Philistines with an ox goad. And he too saved <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl.
